did.abstract: This collection documents history, campus administration, and events of The College of Saint Rose in Albany, New York, founded in 1920 and closed in 2024. Despite the dates, the collection does not contain administrative materials encompassing the entirety of the college's history and the College of St. Rose did not donate administrative records from its last decade to the archives.
did.physloc: The materials are located onsite in the department.

scopecontent.head: Content Description
scopecontent.p: This collection includes institutional records of the College of St. Rose including the Office of the President, Vice President for Academic Affairs, course catalogs, various academic departments, alumni materials, yearbooks, and publications.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: The collection was initially inventoried in 2025 by Maggie Zehr. Five series (Office of the President, Office of the Vice President, Office of the Registrar, Publications and Alumni Materials) were processed in 2025 by Kathy Merring-Darling.

accessrestrict.head: Conditions Governing Access
accessrestrict.p: Access to the five processed series in the collection is unrestricted with the exception of any files specifically noted on the finding aid as they contain personally idetifiable information. Unprocssed series remain restricted. Please contact an archivist for more details.

acqinfo.head: Immediate Source of Acquisition
acqinfo.p: Sister Honora Kinney, college archivist, facilitated the donation of all items in this collection on behalf of the College of St. Rose to the M.E. Grenander Department of Special Collections and Archives in October 2024.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: The collection is arranged into twelve series. Five of them (Office of the President, Office of the Vice President, Office of the Registrar, Publications and Alumni Materials) are processed. All are arranged alphabetically except for the subseries Publications, Student Handbooks; Publications, Student Publications; and Alumni Materials, Directory which are arranged chronologically.

bioghist.head: Organizational History
bioghist.p: The College of Saint Rose was a private college located in Albany, New York that opened in 1920. It was initially a Catholic, women only institution that was founded by the Sisters of St. Joseph of Carondelet. The school opened its enrollment to men in the 1969-1970 school year, the same year that the school became independent from the Sisters. The college closed in 2024 following financial difficulties.

relatedmaterial.head: Related Materials
relatedmaterial.p: All archival materials relevant to the Sisters of St. Joseph of Carondelet were transferred by the College of St. Rose to the Carondelet Consolidated Archives in St. Louis, Missouri in 2024. The Albany Institute of History and Art also received historical artifacts, historic garments/textiles, photographs, and printed materials from the College of St. Rose.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The President's papers provide an overview of the activities and events at the College of Saint Rose. The papers include a history of the founding of the college. The papers also highlight the growth of the college over the ensuing decades through the acquistion of property and include materials related to the dedication of new buildings,and the expansion of academic programs. The papers include five decades' worth of faculty meeting minutes that demonstrate the changes the college underwent during this period.

There is also a large amount of materials related to the college's participation in Middle States which is a global institutional accreditor recognized by the United States Secretary of Education. The accreditation process ensures institutional accountability, self-appraisal, improvement and innovation through peer review and the rigorous application of standards within the context of the institutional mission.

The papers also highlight the activities of the Independent College Fund of New York which contains correspondence, newsletters, budget statements, meeting minutes, policy and procedures, and materials regarding the Campaign Fund. The papers related to the college's Five Year Plan also known as Long Range Planning. The inagural materials of three of the college's former president are also included those of Louis Vaccaro, (1983-1996), R. Mark Sullivan, (1996-2012), and David Szczebacki, (2012-2013). The collection also includes materials related to events that occurred at the college such as lectures given by prominent individuals, Rose Day, and commencement programs.

While the majority of the papers associated with the Vice President of Finanace and Academic Affairs consists of meeting minutes.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains materials of the resgistrar's office that include graduate and undergraduate course catalogs. There are also included applications of students who applied to the college in the late 1940s and early 1950s. There are no transcripts or any other materials related to their academic career. The papers include statistics of degrees awarded for both graduate and undergraduate by class and major. There are statistics also for grade distribution by department, summer and evening sessions.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains four subseries - newspapers, yearbooks, student handbooks, and literary magazines and research journals.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Journals and literary magazines include Canary Trills, the Rambler, Xanadu, and the Journal of Undergraduate Research. Le Journal de Marianne a French journal is also included. Canary Trills and the Rambler through 1935 were previously digitized by the College of St. Rose and are available through New York Heritage.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The following newspapers are included in the collection: The Arrow, Rosevaerian, Apocolypse, The Gadfly, Inscape, The Chronicle.

altformavail.head: Copies
altformavail.p: The Albany Public Library also has a set of yearbooks from the College of St. Rose and received a grant to digitize the them. Albany Public has been digitizing the yearbooks and publishing these online with New York Heritage.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Please note there are gaps especially in the 1930s, all of the 1940s and in the 1980s.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The series on Alumni contains five subseries: Administrative, Alumni Directories, Alumni Directory Survey, Alumni Publications, and Memorabilia. The Alumni Directory Survey is the questionnaires that were sent to alumni who wanted to be included in the directory they comprise the year 1989. Memorabilia is made up of several scrapbooks of students, which contain materials realted to their four years at the College of Saint Rose, they contan school ids, photographs, programs, dance cards, tassels, class notes, a textbook, tuition receipts, graduation cards, newspaper clippings, and reunion materials. Each subseries is arranged alphabetically.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The Administrative sub-series contains the institutional materials of the Alumni Association and the Office of Alumni Relations which has records from reunions, constitution and bylaws, fundraising files, scholarship materials, and the records of the student loan fund.
